---
# =============================================================================
# SOP TEMPLATE -- Copy this file to create a new SOP
# =============================================================================
#
# ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
# │                    CONTRIBUTOR DIRECTIONS                          │
# │                                                                     │
# │  READ THIS ENTIRE HEADER BEFORE WRITING OR EDITING ANY SOP.        │
# │                                                                     │
# │  This template defines the required structure for all SOPs in the  │
# │  EA Program Biogeochemistry Lab SOP system. Every section below    │
# │  is mandatory unless explicitly marked OPTIONAL. Do not skip       │
# │  sections; if a section does not apply, leave it with a brief      │
# │  note explaining why (e.g., "Not applicable -- computational       │
# │  procedure with no physical hazards.").                            │
# └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
#
# ── BEFORE YOU START ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   1. CONFIRM THE SOP NUMBER AND SCOPE WITH PROFESSOR MARC LOS HUERTOS
#      before doing any writing. Send him a short description (2--3
#      sentences) of what the SOP will cover, the proposed SOP number,
#      and the proposed title. Do not proceed until he approves.
#
#   2. Pull the latest changes from the repository:
#
#         git pull origin master
#
#      This ensures you are working from the most current files and
#      avoids merge conflicts.
#
#   3. Copy this template into the correct directory:
#
#      Field SOPs:  cp field_sops/SOP-TEMPLATE.qmd field_sops/SOP-FXXX-short-name.qmd
#      Lab SOPs:    cp lab_sops/SOP-TEMPLATE.qmd lab_sops/SOP-LXXX-short-name.qmd
#      General:     cp sops/SOP-TEMPLATE.qmd sops/SOP-XXX-short-name.qmd
#
# ── NAMING CONVENTION ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   SOP-[prefix][number]-[short-description].qmd
#
#   Prefix: F = field, L = lab (omit for general SOPs)
#   Number: Use the numbering scheme in index.qmd
#   Short description: lowercase, hyphens, no spaces
#
#   Examples:
#     SOP-F401-soil-texture-by-feel.qmd
#     SOP-L414-soil-ea-irms.qmd
#     SOP-F602-inaturalist.qmd
#
# ── REQUIRED ELEMENTS (CHECKLIST) ────────────────────────────────────
#
#   Before pushing your SOP, verify ALL of the following:
#
#   [ ] Title, SOP number, and scope approved by Prof. Los Huertos
#   [ ] All sections present (Purpose through Training Record)
#   [ ] Definitions section included (Section 4 or 5) with all
#       technical terms defined and cited where appropriate
#   [ ] References use BibTeX: all citations are @key entries from
#       references.bib, and the References section uses ::: {#refs} :::
#   [ ] New BibTeX entries appended to references.bib (not inline)
#   [ ] BibTeX keys use the key Google Scholar generates (LastnameYYYY)
#   [ ] Related SOPs listed with working Quarto cross-reference links
#   [ ] Images saved as PNG in images/ using SOP-FXXX_descriptor.png
#       naming convention, cropped and compressed to under 500 KB
#   [ ] index.qmd has NOT been modified (Marc will update it)
#   [ ] File previews correctly: quarto preview
#   [ ] Git pull performed before AND after committing
#
# ── GIT WORKFLOW ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   1. git pull origin master          # ALWAYS pull first
#   2. [create or edit your .qmd file]
#   3. quarto preview                  # verify it renders
#   4. git add field_sops/SOP-FXXX-short-name.qmd references.bib images/SOP-FXXX_*.png
#   5. git commit -m "F401: added soil texture SOP with bibtex refs"
#   6. git pull origin master          # pull again before pushing
#   7. git push origin master          #   (or open a Pull Request)
#
#   If step 6 reveals conflicts, resolve them before pushing.
#   NEVER force-push to master.
#
# ── DO NOT EDIT index.qmd ───────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   Professor Los Huertos maintains index.qmd. After your SOP is
#   merged, he will add the entry to the index table. If you believe
#   the index needs updating, open a GitHub Issue or email him.
#
# ── BIBTEX REQUIREMENTS ─────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   All SOPs must use BibTeX citations from references.bib. Do NOT
#   write plain-text reference lists. The project-level _quarto.yml
#   sets bibliography: references.bib and csl: apa.csl globally.
#
#   To cite in the text:       @kalra1998 or [@kalra1998; @jones2001]
#   To render the reference list, use the div at the end:
#
#     ## N. References
#
#     ::: {#refs}
#     :::
#
#   To add a new reference:
#     1. Search Google Scholar (scholar.google.com) for the work
#     2. Click the "Cite" link (quotation mark icon) below the result
#     3. At the bottom of the citation popup, click "BibTeX"
#     4. Copy the entire entry that appears
#     5. Paste it into references.bib (at the end of the file, or
#        grouped near other entries for the same SOP)
#     6. Clean up the entry using the guidelines below
#     7. Check references.bib for duplicates (search for the author
#        surname and year) before saving
#     8. Commit references.bib alongside your SOP file
#
#   KEY STYLE: Keep the citation key that Google Scholar generates.
#   Google Scholar keys follow the pattern LastnameYYYY (e.g.,
#   wright2004, chen1997, herrick2005). Do not invent your own keys.
#   If two entries share the same key, append a letter:
#   reich2014a, reich2014b.
#
#   CLEANING UP A GOOGLE SCHOLAR ENTRY:
#
#   Google Scholar BibTeX output is often messy. Fix the following:
#
#     - Remove curly braces around the entire title (keep only those
#       protecting capitalization of proper nouns or acronyms):
#         BAD:   title = {{The worldwide leaf economics spectrum}}
#         GOOD:  title = {The worldwide leaf economics spectrum}
#         GOOD:  title = {Forest Inventory and Analysis ({FIA}) guide}
#
#     - Add the DOI field if missing (look it up on doi.org or the
#       publisher's website):
#         doi = {10.1038/nature02403}
#
#     - Standardize field names to lowercase: title, author, journal,
#       volume, number, pages, year, doi, publisher, address
#
#     - Use and (not &) between author names
#
#     - Add a note field if the entry supports a specific SOP context:
#         note = {Leaf trait protocols for standardized sampling}
#
#   EXAMPLE -- a clean BibTeX entry ready for references.bib:
#
#     @article{wright2004,
#       title     = {The worldwide leaf economics spectrum},
#       author    = {Wright, Ian J. and Reich, Peter B. and Westoby,
#                    Mark and Ackerly, David D. and Baruch, Zdravko
#                    and Bongers, Frans and others},
#       journal   = {Nature},
#       volume    = {428},
#       pages     = {821--827},
#       year      = {2004},
#       doi       = {10.1038/nature02403}
#     }
#
#   COMMON ENTRY TYPES:
#
#     @article{key, ...}        Journal article (most common)
#     @book{key, ...}           Book (add publisher, address)
#     @incollection{key, ...}   Book chapter (add booktitle, editor)
#     @techreport{key, ...}     Agency report (add institution)
#     @misc{key, ...}           Websites, software, datasets
#
# ── IMAGE REQUIREMENTS ───────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   Images are stored in the images/ directory at the project root.
#   All images must be PNG format.
#
#   Naming convention:
#
#     SOP-[prefix][number]_descriptor.png
#
#   Use the SOP number, an underscore, and a short lowercase
#   descriptor with underscores separating words. Examples:
#
#     SOP-F401_ribbon_test.png
#     SOP-F401_textural_triangle.png
#     SOP-L414_tin_capsule_loading.png
#     SOP-F604_dbh_tape_placement.png
#     SOP-F606_densiometer_reading.png
#
#   To include an image in your SOP:
#
#     ![Short caption describing the image.](../images/SOP-F401_ribbon_test.png){width=80%}
#
#   Notes:
#     - The path is relative to the .qmd file location (field_sops/
#       or lab_sops/), so use ../images/ to reach the shared images/
#       directory.
#     - Set width to 60--80% for most procedural photos. Use 100%
#       only for wide diagrams or data sheets.
#     - Add a descriptive alt-text caption inside the square brackets;
#       this is required for accessibility and appears in the PDF.
#     - Crop and compress images before committing. Target file size
#       is under 500 KB per image. Use a tool like ImageMagick:
#
#         convert input.jpg -resize 1200x1200\> -quality 85 SOP-F401_ribbon_test.png
#
#     - Do not commit raw camera photos (3--10 MB each). Resize first.
#     - Commit images alongside your .qmd file:
#
#         git add images/SOP-F401_ribbon_test.png field_sops/SOP-F401-soil-texture-by-feel.qmd
#
#     - For figures generated by R code chunks, let Quarto handle the
#       output automatically (do not save and reference manually).
#     - When adapting photos taken by others, credit the photographer
#       in the caption or a footnote.
#
# ── WRITING STYLE ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
#   - Use US spelling throughout
#   - Avoid em-dashes; use commas, semicolons, or parentheses instead
#   - Write in imperative mood for procedural steps ("Collect...",
#     "Record...", "Measure...")
#   - Use SI units; spell out units on first use, then abbreviate
#   - Define all technical terms in the Definitions section
#   - Use Quarto callout boxes for tips, warnings, and important notes
#   - Embed R code chunks for calculations where helpful
#   - Be specific: include settings, volumes, durations, and
#     instrument model numbers
#
# =============================================================================

title: "Title of Procedure"
sop-number: "SOP-XXX"
author:
  - name: "Your Name"
    affiliation: "EA Program, Pomona College"
approved-by: "Marc Los Huertos"
date: last-modified
date-format: "YYYY-MM-DD"
revision: "0.1"

revision-history:
  - version: "0.1"
    date: "YYYY-MM-DD"
    author: "Your Name"
    changes: "Initial release"
# - version: "0.2"
#   date: "YYYY-MM-DD"
#   author: "Another Person"
#   changes: "Updated step 3 to reflect new equipment; added bibtex refs"
---

## 5. Safety and Hazards

- **Chemical:** [e.g., corrosive reagents, toxic fumes]
- **Biological:** [e.g., soil-borne pathogens, ticks, poison oak]
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses / goggles
- [ ] Lab coat or field-appropriate clothing
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] [Other PPE as needed]

### Required Training

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd) or
